controls.rule: Pin provider/dependencies/patches/licenses; build-time provider only; no system TLS fallback; signed SBOM/artifacts.
Validate chain and reference identity by default; SNI/DNS/IP/trust are distinct; no public TrustAll.
Private keys remain opaque; external signer and RNG failures are fail-closed; no secret/provider handle escapes.
Immutable contexts disable obsolete/insecure TLS features and reject unsupported capabilities before networking.
One monotonic OperationContext; typed EOF/close/abort/cancel/truncation; exactly-once terminal and cleanup.
Resolver/attempt queues are bounded; origin/proxy DNS, network binding and route evidence remain distinct.
HTTP/1 parser/serializer share strict framing; reject CL/TE ambiguity, obs-fold, CRLF and invalid chunks.
Validate HTTP/2 frame/state ordering and bound HPACK, continuation, window, stream and write queues.
Pool/session keys include origin, proxy, network, TLS context, trust, client identity, provider and ALPN.
Default logs exclude keys, traffic/session secrets, credentials and bodies; release builds cannot key-log.
Validate callback lengths/ownership; translate exceptions; no user callback under global provider locks.
Trust/key/network capabilities require native device/VM evidence and fail closed when unavailable.
Evidence binds commit/toolchain/target/native runner/artifact digests; skipped/stale/cross-compile cannot PASS.

threats.scenario: Compromised provider source/dependency/patch enters all release artifacts.
threats.residual: Pinned upstream can still contain an undiscovered vulnerability.

threats.scenario: Runtime loader selects hostile or stale system libssl/libcrypto/provider modules.
threats.residual: Transitive native dependencies still require per-artifact scans.

threats.scenario: Expired, untrusted, malformed or policy-incompatible certificate chain is accepted.
threats.residual: Platform trust policy differences must remain visible evidence.

threats.scenario: CN fallback, wildcard/IDNA, DNS/IP or SNI/reference confusion authenticates the wrong peer.
Private key bytes, signer authority, entropy or provider handles escape the opaque key boundary.
threats.residual: OS keystore compromise is outside Wirestack.

threats.scenario: Provider defaults or leaked configuration enable downgrade, obsolete protocol or insecure features.
threats.residual: Provider policy drift requires upgrade regression tests.

threats.scenario: Peer truncation, local close or cancellation is misreported as graceful close_notify/EOF.
threats.residual: Platforms without structured terminal evidence remain blocked.

threats.scenario: Success, timeout, cancel, close and abort race into double completion, UAF or leaked waiters.
threats.residual: Native provider defects still require sanitizers and repeated races.

threats.scenario: Slow DNS blocks carrier threads or grows an unbounded resolver pool/queue.
threats.residual: Opaque platform resolver queues require native stress evidence.

threats.scenario: Origin/proxy DNS, authority or network-binding confusion routes credentials to the wrong endpoint.
threats.residual: OS route changes can race established connections.

threats.scenario: CL/CL, TE/CL, obs-fold, whitespace, CRLF or chunk ambiguity enables request smuggling.
threats.residual: Intermediary differences require continuous differential corpus updates.

threats.scenario: Malformed frame order, CONTINUATION, SETTINGS, pseudo-header or HPACK state corrupts streams.
threats.residual: Cross-frame state remains a high-value fuzz target.

threats.scenario: Attacker-controlled chains, headers, frames, streams or slow bodies grow memory/handles without limit.
threats.residual: Limits require native calibration on small devices.

threats.scenario: Incomplete pool/session key reuses an authenticated channel across trust/identity/proxy/network contexts.
threats.residual: Application identity outside Wirestack cannot be inferred.

threats.scenario: Logs, traces, crash reports or release key logging disclose keys, secrets, credentials or bodies.
threats.residual: Application callbacks can still log their own secrets.

threats.scenario: Malformed lengths, allocator ownership, reentrancy or exceptions crossing C ABI corrupt native memory.
threats.residual: Native code cannot be proven memory-safe by tests alone.

threats.scenario: Platform trust/key/network adapter silently diverges or a cross-compile is labeled native support.
threats.residual: OS policy can change after release.

threats.scenario: Stale, simulated, skipped or cross-compiled evidence authorizes an unsupported release artifact.

release_policy: HIGH/CRITICAL threats may not be ACCEPTED before M7 independent review; unresolved blockers or missing native platforms block stable release.
